whatIsAts.title: What is an ATS (Applicant Tracking System)?
whatIsAts.body: An Applicant Tracking System (ATS) is software that companies use to automatically filter and rank job applications before human recruiters ever see them.

reality.largeCompanies: 75% of large companies use ATS systems to screen applications
reality.fortune500: 98% of Fortune 500 companies rely on ATS for initial screening
reality.resumeRejections: 60-70% of resumes are automatically rejected before human review

whatIsAts.bottomLine: Bottom line: Your resume needs to "speak ATS" to even reach human eyes. ThinkWrite's keyword extraction ensures you're not filtered out by robots.

howItWorks.title: How Does ATS Screening Work?
howItWorks.description: ATS systems scan your resume and assign it a compatibility score based on how well it matches the job posting. Here's the process:

keywordMatching.title: Keyword Matching
keywordMatching.body: Scans for exact skills, technologies, and buzzwords from the job description

formatParsing.title: Format Parsing
formatParsing.body: Attempts to extract contact info, work history, education, and skills

scoreAssignment.title: Score Assignment
scoreAssignment.body: Assigns a numerical score (usually 0-100) based on keyword density and relevance

rankingFiltering.title: Ranking & Filtering
rankingFiltering.body: Only top-scoring resumes (typically 60+ score) reach human recruiters

mistakes.termMismatch: Using different terms than job posting ("JS" vs "JavaScript")
mistakes.missingKeywords: Missing industry buzzwords and required skills

keywords.title: Why Exact Keywords Are Critical
keywords.description: ATS systems look for exact matches between job postings and resumes. Small differences can mean the difference between getting an interview or being automatically rejected.
keywords.advantageBody: Our keyword extraction finds the exact terms used in job postings, ranked by importance. Instead of guessing, you get the precise vocabulary that will maximize your ATS score.

do.exactKeywords: Use exact keywords from job posting
do.acronyms: Include both full names and acronyms (AI and Artificial Intelligence)
do.standardHeaders: Use standard section headers (Experience, Skills, Education)
do.docx: Save as .docx for best ATS compatibility

avoid.tables: Complex tables or columns that break parsing
avoid.headersFooters: Headers and footers (often ignored by ATS)

bottomLine.title: The Bottom Line
bottomLine.body: ATS systems are gatekeepers that determine whether your resume reaches human recruiters. Without proper keyword optimization, even the most qualified candidates get automatically filtered out.
bottomLine.advantage: ThinkWrite's keyword extraction gives you the insider advantage - the exact terms and phrases that will maximize your ATS score and get your resume in front of real people.
